historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved the Phase I plans of Satoru Nishita, of CHNMB Associates, for restoring Huntington Falls at Stow Lake.
Huntington Falls at Stow Lake, restored under a contract with Rock & Waterscape Systems, Inc., was dedicated, as the general manager reported to the Recreation and Park Commission in June 1984.
Thomas U. Sweeny paid for an observatory on the summit of Strawberry Hill, designed by Percy & Hamilton and built in concrete by Ransome & Cushing; a second storey followed in 1891–93.
A contract to grade the first section of the lake around Strawberry Hill was let at 8½ cents a cubic yard; the grading was finished in February 1892 and the bed lined with ten inches of clay.
Work began on Huntington Falls, the cascade from the summit of Strawberry Hill into the lake, paid for by a $25,000 gift from C. P. Huntington and designed by Superintendent John McLaren.
The lake around Strawberry Hill was finished as the park's reservoir, holding 20 to 25 million gallons, high enough to water most of the park by gravity.
The concrete Roman Bridge was built at the northeast corner of Strawberry Hill, carrying the drive to the summit over the lake.
The stone footbridge on the southwest side of Strawberry Hill was added to the plan, because so many people walked out to the lake.
The embankment around the lake was finished with 30,000 cubic yards of sand, with a 25-foot drive carried around it.
The lake bore the name of W. W. Stow, the Park Commission president who had championed it, by the time of his death on February 11, 1895.
The Board of Park Commissioners gave up the boating concession at Stow Lake and ordered the boathouse demolished at once.

Recording the death of their president W. W. Stow, the Park Commissioners told how the lake that bears his name began as a reservoir on the east side of Strawberry Hill, badly needed in case the pumps failed, and was made an ornamental lake at his instance as well, with a pipe from the Almshouse artesian well feeding it without pumping.
